identity.question: What happened, what evidence supports it, and what should we do next?

steps.query: suspicious sign-in after MFA fatigue prompt denial possible account compromise and suspicious endpoint process; contain compromised user account and endpoint

evidence.record: riley.park denied three MFA push prompts, then signed in from 203.0.113.44, a network not seen for this user in 90 days.
FIN-LT-042 launched an unsigned child process from the browser and contacted 203.0.113.44 four minutes after the sign-in.
FIN-LT-042 reaches the Finance App and Data Warehouse through a trusted-device path.
203.0.113.44 is newly observed in this synthetic environment and has no trusted business association.

procedures.title: Endpoint detection isolation
procedures.text: Endpoint detection and response isolation contains a compromised laptop. Capture process evidence, block confirmed indicators, then reimage.

procedures.title: Identity compromise procedure
procedures.text: Procedure for identity takeover: revoke sessions, reset credentials, inspect MFA, isolate the assigned endpoint if execution evidence is present.

procedures.title: Session revocation after takeover
procedures.text: Revoke active sessions, reset credentials, inspect multifactor methods, and preserve timestamps when an identity is suspected compromised.

procedures.title: Endpoint malware procedure
procedures.text: Procedure for endpoint execution: isolate the host, collect process and network evidence, block indicators, and scope related devices.

answer.summary: This appears to be a likely account takeover driven by MFA fatigue: the user denied three MFA prompts and then successfully signed in from a new IP, followed by suspicious execution on the assigned laptop. Contain the account, isolate the laptop, and block the unapproved IP while preserving evidence.

findings.text: riley.park denied three MFA push prompts and then signed in from 203.0.113.44, which was not seen for this user in 90 days.
FIN-LT-042 launched an unsigned child process from the browser and contacted 203.0.113.44 four minutes after the sign-in.
FIN-LT-042 can reach the Finance App and Data Warehouse through a trusted-device path, so compromise of this laptop could impact sensitive finance systems.
203.0.113.44 is newly observed in this environment and has no trusted business association.

actions.rationale: The user showed MFA fatigue behavior followed by a new sign-in from an unfamiliar IP, consistent with possible takeover.
The successful sign-in after repeated MFA denials indicates the account should be reset as part of takeover containment.
Unsigned browser-launched execution and immediate contact to the same IP indicate likely endpoint compromise.
The IP is newly observed with no trusted business association and is tied to the suspicious sign-in and host contact.

cloud.question: What happened, what evidence supports it, and what should we do next?

steps.query: suspicious unusual Data Warehouse read volume by service account using external IP and service credential; need contain possible credential misuse and data access investigation

evidence.record: service.finance issued tokens to 198.51.100.18, outside the service's approved deployment range.
PUBLIC-API made 1,240 Data Warehouse read calls in ten minutes using the service credential.
198.51.100.18 belongs to a hosting range with no approved integration in this synthetic environment.
PUBLIC-API reaches the Data Warehouse through the Identity Gateway and Finance App.

procedures.title: Cloud credential rotation
procedures.text: Disable the exposed service credential, rotate dependent secrets, review warehouse reads, and preserve cloud audit logs before any remediation.

procedures.title: Data warehouse access review
procedures.text: Warehouse access reviews list every identity with read or write roles. Standing write access should be removed unless a ticket justifies it.

procedures.title: Cloud credential procedure
procedures.text: Procedure for leaked cloud keys: disable the credential, rotate secrets, review data access, and keep audit evidence.

procedures.title: Least privilege for warehouse roles
procedures.text: Remove standing write access to the data warehouse. Finance applications should use least privilege roles reviewed quarterly.

answer.summary: PUBLIC-API appears to have used the service.finance credential from an unapproved external IP to generate a burst of Data Warehouse reads, indicating likely service-account misuse. The evidence supports immediate credential containment and blocking the unapproved source while preserving logs for review.

findings.text: service.finance issued tokens to 198.51.100.18, and that IP is in a hosting range with no approved integration in this environment.
PUBLIC-API made 1,240 Data Warehouse read calls in ten minutes using the service credential.
PUBLIC-API has reachability to the Data Warehouse through the Identity Gateway and Finance App, so this host is on the access path to the affected system.

actions.rationale: The service credential was used from an unapproved external IP and drove high-volume warehouse reads.
Trusted intel shows the IP is in a hosting range with no approved integration in this environment.

HR-LT-208 opened payroll-verify.example from the mail client at 09:12 and submitted a login form. No downloads or new processes followed.
payroll-verify.example was registered three days ago, imitates the company payroll portal, and is not on any approved sender or partner list.
HR-LT-208 has no path to critical data. morgan.lee holds read access to the HR payroll application.
192.0.2.77 hosts several newly registered lookalike domains and has no business association.

answer.summary: This looks like a credential-phishing event: the user visited a lookalike payroll site, submitted a login form, and then a new session appeared for the account from an unfamiliar IP. The host shows no post-login execution activity, so containment should focus on identity and indicator blocking.

findings.text: HR-LT-208 opened the payroll-verify.example link from email and submitted a login form, with no downloads or new processes afterward.

morgan.lee had a new session created from 192.0.2.77 two minutes after the site visit, and that network had never been seen for the user.
payroll-verify.example was registered three days ago, imitates the company payroll portal, and is not on any approved sender or partner list.

actions.rationale: A new session appeared immediately after the login submission from an unfamiliar network, consistent with account compromise.
The user likely entered credentials into a lookalike payroll site.
Trusted intel shows this is a recent payroll lookalike domain and it is not approved.
Trusted intel associates the IP with newly registered lookalike domains and no business association.

steps.query: impossible-travel alert caused by approved VPN provider egress and compliant device phishing-resistant MFA benign sign-in review

procedures.text: Require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for privileged users. FIDO2 security keys replace SMS and push prompts. Enrollment is handled at the identity gateway.

procedures.text: Require device compliance and phishing-resistant MFA before the identity gateway issues a finance application session.

procedures.title: Authentication overview

answer.summary: The alert is explained by a legitimate VPN egress from Frankfurt on an enrolled, compliant device rather than account compromise. Evidence does not show host compromise or access to sensitive data, so no containment is warranted.

findings.text: dana.ortiz’s sign-in from 198.18.0.25 occurred on the same enrolled, compliant device as the earlier sign-in and passed phishing-resistant MFA.
198.18.0.25 is an approved VPN provider egress address for the company’s Frankfurt point of presence, which explains the geography shift.
